title: Box Four
alt: Four panels. Panel 1: in the teal office, the supply closet door stands open beside a sign reading SUPPLIES. Inside, shelves of coloured boxes run back much further than the wall could possibly allow. Pip, a small lavender candle-ghost with a flame on top, floats out of the doorway hugging a fat new ream of forms in a brown paper band. Margo, a tall caseworker with a grey bun, round glasses and a mustard cardigan, stands beside the door holding her mug, deadpan. Panel 2: closer. Pip holds up a single sheet, eyes wide and mouth open. Margo sips beside them, half-lidded, not looking. Panel 3: close-up of the printed form. Under a teal header, FORM 1 · CASE CLOSURE, 'Closed by:' lists three printed tick boxes: STAMPED, EXCEEDS SMALL (REFER UP), and FOUND BY REQUESTER. A lavender Pip hand points at the last one. At the bottom: 'Approved: H.' Panel 4: Pip holds the form up high, beaming up at Margo. Margo faces away toward the closet, deadpan. Tucked into the back of her bun is one blank copy of the new form, folded, its teal header showing.
hover: Forty years for a comma. One week for a box.
transcript: Panel 1 – PIP: The new forms came.
Panel 1 – MARGO: They reprint them every forty years. To move a comma.
Panel 2 – PIP: They didn't move a comma.
Panel 3 – (silent. The form reads: FORM 1 · CASE CLOSURE. Closed by: STAMPED / EXCEEDS SMALL (REFER UP) / FOUND BY REQUESTER. Approved: H.)
Panel 4 – PIP: Margo, they printed my box!
Panel 4 – (Margo says nothing. A blank copy of the form is tucked into her bun.)
note: A week ago Pip drew a box on a form by hand. Somebody upstairs was reading.
